title: Pushouts, Pullbacks, and Interface Composition
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in category theory/algebra, centered on the claim that systems compose by explicit shared interfaces and universal compatibility conditions. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that interface composition can be made exact without asserting identical internal representations. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: set-level pullback/pushout, interface gluing example, and universal property.

title: Universal Properties and Adjunctions as Interface-First Characterization
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in category theory, centered on the claim that objects may be characterized by the lawful maps they admit rather than by one privileged internal construction. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that interface-first reasoning is standard mathematics when backed by a universal property. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: free/forgetful example, product/coproduct example, and adjunction terminology discipline.

title: Cantor Diagonalization as Non-Exhaustiveness
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in set theory/logic, centered on the claim that a purported exhaustive representation admits a construction that escapes it. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that non-surjectivity and non-exhaustiveness are rigorous controls; they do not establish a general transfinite Boundary architecture. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: Cantor theorem, diagonal construction, and explicit non-generalization firewall.

title: Recursive Definition and Mathematical Induction as Lawful Generation
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in logic/discrete mathematics, centered on the claim that a base case plus lawful recursive constructor generates a closed family under explicit formation rules. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that recursive-system language should reduce to standard recursion and induction where those are sufficient. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: recursive datatype or sequence, induction proof, and ill-founded counterexample.

title: Gauss–Bonnet as Local-to-Global Accounting
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in differential geometry/topology, centered on the claim that local curvature, global topology, and explicit boundary correction participate in one exact invariant relation. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that local-to-global Boundary language can be calibrated against a theorem with explicit boundary terms. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: closed-surface theorem, surface-with-boundary form, and geodesic-curvature term.

title: Voronoi and Delaunay Structures as Boundary Formation
summary: This paper candidate develops “Voronoi and Delaunay Structures as Boundary Formation” from material already present in the Lab corpus. Its current claim ceiling is the core object is standard and exact, allowing a low-risk Boundary reading if the paper removes unsupported shell/cognitive claims and returns the interpretation to ordinary computational geometry. The current artifact state is legacy manuscript candidate re-routed through current publication controls. The next evidence obligation is competition-induced interface formation as a canonical discrete calibration; Voronoi/Delaunay duality as region/interface vs adjacency representation. Prior to promotion, it requires review against native theorem/definition audit, weighted/geodesic scope check, one positive and one failure/degeneracy case.
